skill.name: cinematic-shot-prompting
skill.description: Turn a scene goal, storyboard, or reference image into a camera movement prompt for AI video generation. Revise prompts when subjects drift, backgrounds jump, or the camera takes the wrong path.
skill.summary: Write and refine AI video prompts with clear camera paths, framing, focus, and keyframe guidance.

content.value_statement: Vague video prompts leave the camera path, subject framing, and final composition open to guesswork. Turn a scene goal or reference image into specific motion instructions, then revise them based on what the generated shot gets wrong.
actual_capabilities: Choose a primary camera move from 40 shot patterns based on what the viewer should notice.
Specify start and end framing, camera path and speed, subject stability, and how the background should respond.
Separate camera movement from changes in lens zoom or focus to resolve conflicting instructions.
Check whether a supplied reference image shows enough space, depth, or foreground detail for the planned move.
Suggest start, end, and intermediate keyframes for shots that cross spaces or change scale.
Diagnose visible problems such as subject drift or background jumps and revise the relevant part of the prompt.
limitations: The skill writes instructions and suggests keyframes. It does not render video or generate reference images.
Results depend on the video model and the available references. A precise prompt cannot guarantee consistent motion.
Text alone cannot supply missing geometry for a complex camera path.
The skill does not handle static image prompts, editing, color grading, audio, or model selection.

use_cases.title: Direct Attention in a Narrative Scene
use_cases.description: Turn a storyboard beat into one clear camera move with a defined start, pace, and final focus.

use_cases.title: Reveal a Product Without Losing Its Label
use_cases.description: Plan a sideways camera move that clears a foreground obstruction and ends with the product and its label visible.

use_cases.title: Repair a Drifting Generated Shot
use_cases.description: Use the original prompt and a failure description to revise the camera path or continuity constraints without rewriting the entire shot.

prompt_templates.title: Write a Slow Push-In
prompt_templates.prompt: Write one video prompt that moves from a medium shot of [subject] to a close-up of [detail]. Keep the subject centered and describe how the camera slows to a stop.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: Turn a clear shot idea into a single motion prompt.

prompt_templates.title: Reveal a Subject From a Reference Image
prompt_templates.prompt: Use my reference image to reveal [subject] from behind [foreground object]. Choose a camera direction and describe how the foreground moves relative to the background. End with [detail] clearly visible.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: Use an existing image to plan a foreground reveal.

prompt_templates.title: Fix an Unintended Zoom
prompt_templates.prompt: My prompt was [original prompt], but the clip only zooms in. Rewrite it so the camera moves toward [subject] at a fixed focal length. Keep the rest of the shot unchanged.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: Revise a prompt after observing a specific generation failure.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Continuous Doorway Shot
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a continuous camera move from [start space] through [doorway] to [final subject]. Describe the start and end frames, plus any intermediate frame needed to keep the route clear. Suggest separate shots if the spaces cannot connect.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: Plan reference frames for a move between two spaces.

output_examples.input: From a medium shot of a seated person, move closer and finish on their eyes.
output_examples.output: Move the camera straight toward the seated person over six seconds, keeping the focal length fixed. Keep the person centered and their head steady. Let nearby objects shift outward faster than the far wall. Slow to a stop on a close-up with both eyes in focus.

output_examples.input: Move from a garden path through an open greenhouse door and finish on a seedling.
output: Shot choice: Use a straight push through the doorway to connect the two spaces.

Prompt: Start on the garden path facing the open door. Glide forward through the center of the doorway at a steady height. Keep the potting bench aligned in the distance, then slow to a stop with the seedling centered and sharp.
Keyframes: Start with the full doorway visible. Add a threshold frame with the bench ahead, then finish on the seedling.

best_practices: State what the viewer should notice first, then choose one primary move to direct that attention.
Use the reference image for appearance and the prompt for movement. Specify what changes, what stays fixed, and where the shot ends.
Test one targeted revision at a time. Add reference frames or split the shot when the path lacks spatial detail.
anti_patterns: Relying on mood words instead of specifying camera direction, speed, or final framing.
Combining incompatible moves, such as lifting the camera while asking for a fixed position.
Adding more adjectives when the reference does not show a clear route or destination.

faq.question: Can I use the skill without a reference image?
faq.answer: Yes. Describe the subject, its action, and the setting so the skill can write the shot around them.

faq.question: Does the skill generate the video?
faq.answer: No. It writes and revises the prompt. You run that prompt in a separate video generator.

faq.question: What is the difference between a push-in and a zoom?
faq.answer: A push-in moves the camera and changes perspective. A zoom changes the field of view while the camera stays in place.

faq.question: When should I use more than one keyframe?
faq.answer: Use start and end frames for complex transitions. Add an intermediate frame when the path between them is unclear.

faq.question: Can the skill fix a clip with a drifting subject or a jumping background?
faq.answer: It can suggest prompt or reference changes based on the visible failure. It does not edit the clip directly.

faq.question: Will the same prompt work in every video generator?
faq.answer: The prompts use general camera language, but generators interpret motion differently. Test and adjust the prompt in your chosen tool.
